hook: Placeholder hook for the test fixture: two countries have the same population today, but one will double in 35 years and the other will shrink. The difference is in two numbers: births and deaths per 1,000 people.

prereq.q: Placeholder: what does the rule of 70 give?
prereq.why: Placeholder: 70 over the growth rate is the doubling time.

prereq.q: Placeholder: what does a wide-based population pyramid show?
prereq.why: Placeholder: the base holds the youngest cohort.

chain.effect: gives the growth rate in percent

ideas: Placeholder: crude rates are per 1,000 people, so divide their difference by 10 for a percent.
Placeholder: doubling time is about 70 divided by the growth rate in percent.

misconception.wrong: Placeholder: a 2% growth rate means 2 more people.
misconception.right: Placeholder: 2% means 2 more people for every 100 each year.

summary: Placeholder summary: the rate of natural increase is the crude birth rate minus the crude death rate, divided by 10; the rule of 70 turns it into a doubling time.
